successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: Jambi, annexed into the Palembang Residency in 1903; Sultan Taha killed in 1904

ledger.x: 1460: Datuk Paduko Berhalo founds the Kingdom of Jambi.

c. 1615: the kingdom becomes a sultanate. 'At around 1615, Jambi became a sultanate'; the English and Dutch trading posts date to the same time and by 1616 Jambi was 'the second-largest Sumatran port after Aceh'.
1655: Tungkal passes from Jambi to Johor. the Johor-Jambi wars page lists 1655: a pro-Johor rebellion forced Jambi out of Tungkal; in 1629 Johor had asked for Tungkal back and Jambi kept it.

May 1667: the Johor-Jambi war begins at sea and on the coast. the page's May 1667 entry: a Johorese fleet destroyed fishing huts and orchards at the mouth of the Jambi River; the page puts the first clash near Lingga in 1666 (with Palembang) and the Jambi raid on Indragiri and Tungkal in August 1670.

1679-1681: the war ends with Jambi back on its coast. in May 1679 Johor attacked Jambi with 300 ships and Jambi paid 10,000 rijksdaalders and sent two hostages; then, with VOC support, Jambi recaptured Kuala Tungkal and Indragiri and Daeng Mangika was killed (undated; the page's infobox lists a fourth war 1680-1681 as…

c. 1681: Jambi recovers Tungkal. The Johor-Jambi wars page says Jambi 'unexpectedly countered the Johor-Palembang-Bugis attacks and recaptured Kuala Tungkal and Indragiri' and its text ends the war on that recapture. The page gives no year (the infobox lists 'Recapture of Kuala Tungkal' among the results of the 1673…
1688: the VOC deposes Sultan Ingalaga and Jambi divides.
1858: a Dutch expedition deposes Sultan Taha and Jambi divides again.
1903-1904: the Dutch absorb Jambi. the page has Jambi annexed into the Palembang Residency in 1903; Taha was killed in 1904 (Thaha page: 'killed in 1904 by Dutch soldiers' at Betung Bedarah).

1904: the Jambi Sultanate ends with the death of Sultan Taha. the page says Taha's killing marked the end of the sultanate; infobox 'Disestablished: 1904'; a caption dates the crown prince's surrender of the insignia to 26 March 1904.

wars.name: Johor-Jambi wars
wars.outcome: Jambi burned Johor's capital on 4 April 1673 and was beaten in 1679 (300 Johor ships; 10,000 rijksdaalders, two cannons and two hostages); with VOC help it then recovered Kuala Tungkal and Indragiri and Daeng Mangika was killed.

wars.name: Dutch conquest of Jambi
wars.outcome: 1833: Sultan Mohammad Fakhruddin invaded Dutch-controlled Palembang and was forced to accept Dutch authority and concessions; 1858: a Dutch expedition deposed Taha and installed Ahmad Nazaruddin; 1903: annexation into the Palembang Residency; 1904: Taha…

certainty.note: A river domain ('Jambi with its nine rivers') whose upland edges (Sungai Tenang, Serampas, Kerinci) were autonomous; no treaty line is on the pages, even for the Dutch period.
